summary: Defines BUNDLE, an extension to the Session Description Protocol that lets several media streams, such as audio and video, share a single transport connection instead of using one each. It builds on the SDP offer/answer mechanism and adds related RTP Control Protocol items. Sharing a connection reduces the number of ports and NAT or firewall pinholes needed. It obsoletes RFC 8843.

plainLanguage.summary: This document lets a call carry its audio, video and other media over one network connection instead of one connection per stream. It defines how the two ends agree, in the session description they exchange, which media will share a connection, and how the media is labelled so each stream still reaches the right application.

questions: how to send audio and video over one port
what is the mid rtp header extension
how does bundle choose the tagged media section
subtitle: How several media streams in a session description share one network connection instead of one each.

tldr.problem: When the offer/answer mechanism negotiates a multimedia session with a separate transport for each media stream, each one consumes extra resources, especially when Interactive Connectivity Establishment is used to find the path to each host.
tldr.mechanism: The BUNDLE extension lists the identification tags of the media sections that belong together in an SDP group attribute. One tagged section supplies the address, port and attributes for the whole group, and a new MID item in RTP and RTCP carries the tag inside the media so streams can still be told apart.
tldr.outcome: This document replaced RFC 8843, aligning the port assignment rules with RFC 8829 and clearing up an inconsistency between the two. It also adds the bundle-only attribute and the MID RTP header extension.

today: RFC 9143 is a Proposed Standard that replaced RFC 8843. The metadata for this RFC lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Media Is Bundled
sections.content:
When the SDP offer/answer mechanism is used to negotiate the establishment of a multimedia session, negotiating a separate transport for each individual media stream consumes additional resources, especially when Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) is used. Using a single transport for multiple media streams is therefore attractive.

This specification defines a way to use a single transport, the BUNDLE transport, for sending and receiving media described by multiple SDP media descriptions, the 'm=' sections. The address and port an endpoint uses for sending and receiving that media is the BUNDLE address:port, and the set of SDP attributes applied to each 'm=' section within a BUNDLE group is the BUNDLE attributes. Because the same transport is used for sending and receiving, the symmetric RTP mechanism is always used for RTP-based bundled media.

The specification defines a new SDP Grouping Framework extension called BUNDLE, which the offerer and answerer use with the offer/answer mechanism to negotiate which 'm=' sections become part of a BUNDLE group, which address and port the group uses, and which BUNDLE attributes apply to each section in the group. A single set of ICE candidates can then be used for the whole group.

A given BUNDLE address:port must only be associated with a single BUNDLE group. Offers and answers may contain several BUNDLE groups, and the procedures apply to each group independently. All RTP-based bundled media associated with a given group belong to a single RTP session.

The extension is backward compatible. Endpoints that do not support it are expected to generate offers and answers without a BUNDLE group attribute and to assign a unique address and port to each 'm=' section, as the base offer/answer rules require.
sections.plainLanguage: Negotiating a separate network connection for every media stream uses up extra resources, especially when the network has to discover the best route for each one. This document lets several streams share a single connection, and defines how the two ends agree on that in the session description.

sections.title: The Vocabulary of BUNDLE
sections.content:
The document defines its terms precisely. An 'm=' section is an SDP media description: an 'm=' line together with zero or more attributes associated with it, and each one is assigned a local address and port. A 5-tuple is the collection of source address, source port, destination address, destination port and transport protocol. A unique address:port is one assigned to only a single 'm=' section in an offer or answer.

The offerer BUNDLE-tag is the first identification-tag in the identification-tag list of a group attribute in an offer; the answerer BUNDLE-tag is the same for an answer. The 'm=' section named by the offerer BUNDLE-tag is the offerer-tagged section, and it carries the characteristics, that is the address and port and the attributes, applied to each 'm=' section in the group. The BUNDLE group itself is the set of bundled 'm=' sections that uses a single transport and a single set of BUNDLE attributes for all the media it describes.

A bundled 'm=' section is one whose identification-tag appears in a group:BUNDLE list, and a bundle-only 'm=' section is a bundled section that also carries the bundle-only attribute. An identification-tag is a unique token used to identify an 'm=' section. It is carried in the 'mid' attribute of that section, and the session-level group attribute carries the list of identification-tags that belong to a particular group.
sections.plainLanguage: The document names the parts carefully. The tagged media description is the one whose settings apply to the whole group. The identification-tag is the short name that identifies a media description, and the group attribute lists the tags that belong together.

sections.title: The SDP Grouping Extension
sections.content:
The BUNDLE extension is a new SDP Grouping Framework extension. It is indicated using an SDP group attribute whose semantics value is BUNDLE. An identification-tag is assigned to each bundled 'm=' section, and each identification-tag is listed in the group attribute's identification-tag list. Every 'm=' section whose tag appears in the list is associated with that BUNDLE group.

An SDP body can contain multiple BUNDLE groups, and any given bundled 'm=' section must not be associated with more than one BUNDLE group at any given time. The order of the 'm=' sections listed in the group attribute does not have to match the order in which they appear in the SDP. The multiplexing category for the group attribute is NORMAL.

Beyond the grouping extension, the document defines a new SDP attribute, bundle-only, which asks that a specific 'm=' section be used only if it is kept inside a BUNDLE group. It updates the base offer/answer specification to allow assigning a zero port value to an 'm=' section in cases where the media described is not disabled or rejected. It defines a new RTCP SDES item, Media Identification, and a new RTP SDES header extension that can be used to associate RTP streams with 'm=' sections. It adds an exception, for the MID RTP header extension, to the requirement in RFC 7941 regarding protection of an SDES RTP header extension carrying an SDES item. And it updates the grouping specification so that a group attribute may contain an identification-tag identifying an 'm=' section whose port value is zero.
sections.plainLanguage: The extension is one line in the session description: a group attribute with the value BUNDLE, followed by the list of media sections that belong together. Each section in the list is named by the tag it already carries.

sections.title: The bundle-only Attribute
sections.content:
The bundle-only attribute is a new SDP media-level attribute. It is a property attribute, so it has no value.

Its purpose is to make sure that an answerer which does not support the BUNDLE extension always rejects a bundled 'm=' section in an offer. To do that, the offerer assigns a zero port value to the section, and under the base offer/answer rules an answerer rejects such a section. Including a bundle-only attribute in a bundled 'm=' section asks the answerer to accept the section only if it supports the BUNDLE extension and keeps the section inside the associated BUNDLE group.

The usage of the attribute is only defined for a bundled 'm=' section with a zero port value, and other usage is unspecified. If an offerer or answerer receives a bundle-only attribute in a non-bundled 'm=' section, it must discard the attribute.
sections.plainLanguage: The bundle-only attribute marks a media section that is only acceptable if it travels with the group. The offerer pairs it with a zero port number, which older software would reject, so a peer that does not understand bundling drops that section rather than treat it as separate.

sections.title: The Offer/Answer Procedures
sections.content:
The offer/answer procedures cover negotiating a BUNDLE group, suggesting and selecting the tagged 'm=' sections, adding an 'm=' section to a group, moving one out of a group, and disabling one inside a group. The generic rules of the base offer/answer and grouping specifications also apply, so if an offer is rejected the previously negotiated addresses, parameters and characteristics stand, and a BUNDLE group is not created.

In an initial BUNDLE offer the offerer must assign a unique address and port to each bundled 'm=' section, excluding any bundle-only ones; pick a bundled section as the suggested offerer-tagged section; include the SDP attributes; include the group:BUNDLE attribute; and place the identification-tag of each bundled section in the list, with the offerer BUNDLE-tag first. The offerer must not suggest a bundle-only section as the tagged one, and is recommended to suggest a section the answerer is unlikely to reject or move out of the group. While the answer is outstanding, the offerer has to be prepared to receive bundled media on each unique address and port it assigned.

In the answer, the answerer selects the offerer-tagged 'm=' section and the answerer-tagged 'm=' section, assigns the answerer BUNDLE address and port to the answerer-tagged section and to every other bundled section in the group, and repeats the group:BUNDLE attribute. When choosing the offerer-tagged section the answerer must first check that it will not move the section out of the group, will not reject it, and does not carry a zero port value. If the check fails, it picks the next identification-tag in the offer's list and repeats the check. If there are no tags left it must not create the group. If the answerer does not want to keep a section in the group it must either move it out, by giving it a unique address and port and leaving its tag out of the list, or reject it. A section that was in a previously negotiated group, or one marked bundle-only, cannot be moved out in an answer; an offer is needed for that.

The generic SDP rules also restrict the content of a bundled section. The connection data nettype must be IN and the addrtype must be IP4 or IP6, the same value in each 'm=' section. The BUNDLE attributes, the IDENTICAL and TRANSPORT multiplexing category attributes, appear in every bundled section in the initial offer and only in the tagged section in later offers and in answers; attributes in other categories appear in each bundled section they apply to.
sections.plainLanguage: The offerer suggests one media section to be the one that sets the address and port for the whole group, and the answerer either accepts that choice or moves to the next one in the list. If it accepts no choice, no group is created and each media section keeps its own connection.

sections.title: RTP Streams and the MID Tag
sections.content:
All RTP-based media within a single BUNDLE group belong to a single RTP session, and because a single transport is used for sending and receiving, the symmetric RTP mechanism must be used. The 'm=' sections representing RTP-based media in the group therefore share a single synchronization source numbering space.

A payload type value may be used in more than one bundled 'm=' section only if the codecs behind it share an identical configuration, meaning the same media type, encoding name, clock rate and any parameter that affects the codec configuration and packetization. The proto value in each bundled RTP-based 'm=' section must be identical. The RTP MID header extension must be enabled by including an extmap attribute with the value urn:ietf:params:rtp-hdrext:sdes:mid in every bundled RTP-based 'm=' section in every offer and answer. A given SSRC must not transmit RTP packets using payload types that originate from different bundled 'm=' sections, because sending several media types from one source breaks RTP and RTCP.

Because all the streams in a group share one transport, the local address and port can no longer be used to associate a stream with the right 'm=' section, and several streams may belong to the same section. The document therefore defines a new RTCP SDES item, MID, and a new RTP SDES header extension, which carry the identification-tag of the media section inside the media itself, so a receiver can route each stream to the right section. The MID SDES item should be sent in the first few RTCP packets after joining the session and regularly thereafter, and the header extension should be included in some RTP packets at the start of the session and whenever the SSRC changes. Endpoints must be prepared for the tag to arrive late and should not end the session because of it.
sections.plainLanguage: All the media in a group travels in one RTP session, so the receiver cannot tell the streams apart by the connection they arrived on. The sender therefore writes a short tag into the media itself, so each stream can be matched to the right part of the session description.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations of the base offer/answer and grouping specifications apply to the BUNDLE extension. BUNDLE does not change which information, such as RTP streams, flows over the network, apart from the use of the MID SDES item. It changes which addresses and ports the information flows to, and therefore in which RTP sessions it flows, which affects the security contexts in use and can cause previously separated information flows to share the same security context. Where different security policies would have applied to different bundled streams, or where the parties holding the security contexts would have differed, the implications need further analysis before BUNDLE is selected.

The identification-tag is carried in RTP and RTCP traffic independently of transport, so it can be exposed to parties beyond the signalling chain. The values must therefore be generated so they do not leak user information, for example randomly or with a per-group counter, and should be 3 bytes or fewer so they fit efficiently into the MID RTP header extension. Implementations that generate tags in different ways could be fingerprinted and become targets of specific attacks. Because the tag routes the media to the right application, its integrity and the authenticity of its source matter, and the existing SRTP configurations and other mechanisms that protect the whole RTP and RTCP packets supply that protection.

All the bundled media descriptions must use security configurations that are compatible with one another, so that they can be used at the same time, at least per direction or endpoint. The document adds an exception to RFC 7941 so that the requirement that an SDES header extension be protected with the same strength as the RTCP confidentiality may be ignored for the MID header extension, because no significant security risk is known from leaving it without confidentiality protection.
sections.plainLanguage: Sharing one connection means media that used to have separate protection now shares it, so sites that applied different rules to different streams need to check that first. The tag carried in the media should be random and short, and should not reveal anything about the user.

viz.caption: THE RULES FOR A GROUP OF BUNDLED MEDIA

items.title: One RTP session
items.text: All RTP-based media in a group belong to a single RTP session.

items.title: Symmetric RTP
items.text: The same transport is used for sending and receiving.

items.title: MID extension
items.text: Must be enabled in every bundled RTP-based media section.

items.title: One source per section
items.text: A given SSRC must not send payload types from different sections.

items.title: Payload types
items.text: A value may be reused across sections only if the codecs are configured identically.
